scope: LCS5 (End-of-Life) – Lower heating values for energy substitution
notes: Values are net calorific value (lower heating value, LHV) per kilogram of waste, dry basis.
Use these to convert waste mass sent to incineration into available chemical energy (MJ) before applying plant-specific export efficiencies (XER) from energy_substitution.json.
For mixed MSW fractions, NCV varies widely with moisture; a pragmatic default is provided and should be overridden with plant data if available.

polyurethane_pu.label: Polyurethane (PU, PUR) – generic foam
polyurethane_pu.notes: Within literature, PU foam HHV often ~32–33 MJ/kg; LHV around 20–27 MJ/kg. Using 27.0 MJ/kg as conservative LHV default for flexible/rigid PU.

paper_cardboard.label: Paper & cardboard
paper_cardboard.notes: Approximate NCV for MSW paper/cardboard; effectively air-dry/as‑received. Use plant/lab data if available.

wood_pallet.label: Processed wood / pallets (air‑dry)
wood_pallet.notes: Air‑dry net heat of combustion typically 16.6–19.1 MJ/kg; using 18.0 MJ/kg default.

textiles_biobased.label: Textiles – biobased (cotton, wool, leather)
textiles_biobased.notes: Representative LHV for mixed biobased textiles: Nunes et al. ~16.8; WEC MSW fraction ~19.0. Adjust for moisture if significant.

msw_mixed_residual.label: MSW – mixed residual feed (as‑received)
msw_mixed_residual.notes: Typical as‑received NCV 8–12 MJ/kg in Europe; set 10.0 MJ/kg default. Not truly dry basis; used only if no plant‑specific NCV is available.

electronics.label: Electronics / WEEE (for EF LCS5 electro recycling dataset)
electronics.notes: Handled via dedicated EF EoL dataset (f1de74ac-…); do not apply energy substitution from LHV.

plastics_table12.citation: Juniper Publishers (2018). Energy Potential of Natural, Synthetic Polymers and Waste – Table 12 gives LHV for PE 44.6, PET 23.2, PVC 19.2, PA‑6 30.2, Rubber 42.4 MJ/kg.

wec_table2.citation: World Energy Council (2016). World Energy Resources – Waste to Energy. Table 2: Paper 16, Textiles 19, Plastics 35, Metals 0, Glass 0 MJ/kg (NCV).

wec_residual_range.citation: World Energy Council (2016). Residual waste, unsorted in Europe typically 8–12 MJ/kg NCV (as‑received).

wood_net_dresden.citation: Günther et al. (2012). Calorific value of selected wood species and products – net heat of combustion air‑dry typically 16.6–19.1 MJ/kg.

wood_handbook_note.citation: Eurostat (2012). Quality standard for statistics on wood fuel consumption – bone‑dry GCV ~18–19 MJ/kg; NCV decreases with moisture.

pu_zevenhoven.citation: Zevenhoven. Options for recovery and recycling – LHV ~27 MJ/kg for PU‑based materials (indicative).

pu_range_review.citation: Hasanzadeh et al. (2022). Polyurethane Foam Waste Upcycling – reports PU foam HHV ~32–33 MJ/kg; LHV typically lower ~20–27 MJ/kg.

textile_cotton_lhv.citation: Nunes et al. (2018). Economic and environmental benefits of using textile waste as fuel – LHV ≈ 16.8 MJ/kg for mixed textile waste.

method_standard: EN 15400:2011 / ISO 1928 (conversion to LHV where applicable)

exclusions.note: For these process UUIDs do NOT apply LHV-based energy substitution. Either landfill (no energy) or dedicated EF dataset.
